```{r setup, message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
source("00_load_functions.R")
```

## Design

Compare multi-VAR, adaptive multi-VAR, individual LASSO, and pooled LASSO
using five replications per condition. The baseline has 10 subjects,
20 variables, 100 time points, density 0.05, innovation SD 1, independent
innovations, and no measurement error. Each alternative changes one factor.

| Factor | Levels, including the baseline |
|---|---|
| Innovation SD | 0.5, 1, 2 |
| Number of variables | 10, 20, 30, 40 |
| Nonzero coefficient density | 0.025, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15 |
| Series length | 50, 100 |
| Contemporaneous innovation correlation | 0, 0.3, 0.6 |
| Serial innovation correlation | 0, 0.3, 0.6 |
| Measurement-error SD | 0, 0.5, 1 |

The shared baseline and 15 alternatives give 16 distinct conditions.
Each figure shows six factors; series length is included in the tables.
Knitting reads the saved results.

cat("\n\n")

## Support recovery

```{r support-figures, echo=FALSE, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(c("results/figures/sensitivity.png",
                         "results/figures/specificity.png"))
```

Sensitivity measures recovery of true nonzero coefficients; specificity
measures exclusion of true zeros. Higher values are better for both.
